principle: At the gate, compare finalized GSC and regular organic results before editing. Preserve pages already near page one; prioritize exact-city ownership, wrong-page cannibalization and over-dense architecture on weaker pages.

sitewideFinding.diagnosis: Generic removal intent is spread across many city and specialty pages. Do not repeat broad generic language everywhere; each city page should own its local city intent while national/service hubs own broad non-city intent.

Fresno.diagnosis: Correct page has some relevance but broad Fresno ownership is weak, and prior live SERP evidence showed Clovis/Sanger/Selma pages surfacing for Fresno. High-priority ownership cleanup after the gate.
Fresno.gateDecision: Recheck query-to-page ownership. If sibling cities still rank for Fresno, narrow sibling Fresno references and simplify the Fresno owner to a concise city/process/qualification/local/FAQ/request structure.

Sacramento.diagnosis: Exact Sacramento query remains outside page one even though generic free-pickup signals are stronger. Candidate for city-intent concentration, not a large content expansion.
Sacramento.gateDecision: If exact Sacramento remains ~18, strengthen exact-city ownership and trim nonessential overlap while preserving existing generic top-10 signals.

Anaheim.diagnosis: Page is dense and ranks far better for generic refrigerator intent than local Anaheim removal. Strong candidate for local-intent concentration after the gate.
Anaheim.gateDecision: If local Anaheim terms remain weak, reduce repeated generic/removal sections and retain city-specific process, appliance categories, Anaheim access/utility alternatives, FAQ and request.

Riverside.diagnosis: Overall page is close to page one but local removal intent is weak. Avoid an aggressive rewrite unless post-gate data confirms stalled city ownership.
Riverside.gateDecision: Prefer a surgical ownership cleanup over full rewrite; preserve any top-10 generic free-pickup signals.

Costa Mesa.diagnosis: Strong refrigerator/free-pickup signals but weak local Costa Mesa removal ownership. Candidate for city-intent concentration while protecting refrigerator relevance.
Costa Mesa.gateDecision: Reframe local city sections around pickup/removal intent and keep refrigerator-specific strength in the correct specialty/support pathways.

Irvine.diagnosis: The page earns clicks and useful generic refrigerator visibility, but local Irvine removal intent is weak. Needs ownership concentration, not broad de-optimization.
Irvine.gateDecision: If local Irvine positions remain 30+, simplify city sections and separate Orange County hub language from Irvine owner intent.

Huntington Beach.diagnosis: Overall visibility is close to page one with several strong generic/free/recycling terms, but exact local removal is weak. Protect broad wins and make only surgical local-intent changes if still necessary.
Huntington Beach.gateDecision: Avoid full rewrite if overall position holds; focus on local ownership and CTR.

architecture.note: Legacy Portland document has no <main> wrapper; content is otherwise indexable with H1, canonical, form and 27 H2 sections.

Portland.diagnosis: Legacy structure is unusually dense and semantically old-fashioned. The missing main wrapper is not by itself an indexing failure, so defer markup/body work until the ranking gate unless another audit proves breakage.
Portland.gateDecision: If ranking remains outside top 10, simplify legacy structure substantially while preserving 503 phone, form, official local alternatives, real images and Portland city ownership.

Salem.diagnosis: Despite extremely dense architecture, Salem is already averaging page-one visibility and has clicks. Do not simplify solely because of page length while it is winning.
Salem.gateDecision: Protect if top-10 performance holds. Prefer CTR and exact-city ownership improvements before structural reduction.

measurementRule: Regular organic only for rank evaluation; keep Images, Maps/local pack and AI surfaces separate.
